description: Cheng et al. Multi-ancestry genome-wide association analyses of refractive error augment genetic discovery and polygenic prediction. Nature Genetics, published 20 April 2026. doi:10.1038/s41588-026-02576-0. Licence: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0. A genome-wide association study of refractive error. Add the genes the study names at each associated locus.

proposal.notes: Locus-level table: one row per significant locus, with HGNC nearest protein-coding gene and the HGNC gene list in each locus. Supp Table 9 is a similar lowercase-header loci table that may be an alternative; not verified.

Each row is a GWAS locus for refractive error. Each gene named in Genes_in_locus_ensembl (split on ';') becomes its own edge to the trait, so one locus yields several edges. Entries 'NA' and non-coding placeholders are not resolvable and are skipped by the gene resolver. Genes_in_locus_hgnc is empty and is not used. Locus membership is not a claim that a gene is causal; the edge records only that the study names the gene at the locus. HGNC_nearest_gene is not added separately because it is already within the locus gene list.

proposal.notes: I mapped the nearest protein-coding gene to each locus lead SNP, one gene per row. I did not use Genes_in_locus_ensembl: it is a long list padded with NA, pseudogenes and RNA genes, and those genes are not individually named by the study. The edge keeps the lead SNP and its p-value as properties. The gene-locus link is positional, so the claim is a GWAS statistical association.
